title: Blink Outdoor 4 (1pk System) + Free Blink Video Doorbell (Black) $50 (RRP $237) + Delivery ($0 Prime/ $59 Spend) @ Amazon AU
body:
Deal: Blink Outdoor 4 (1pk System) + Free Blink Video Doorbell (Black) $50 (RRP $237) + Delivery ($0 Prime/ $59 Spend) @ Amazon AU

[Meg4] I hear tepid feedback about this brand. Would I be better off with something like eufy or tp-link?
[Robbo89] We got 2 cameras because it was just $20. The cameras are fine. The software is dogshit. It literally prompts constantly with "continue?" to watch a camera… if you don't press it then it stops. And it only goes away for like 20 seconds.
[jimojr] I think it's mainly to save battery. Otherwise, how could just 2 AA batteries last for a year?
[netsurfer] You get what you paid for. These are cheap for a reason.
Even if you use local storage (sync module 2 with USB stick), from the app, it is still via cloud (so it goes mobile phone to Blink cloud then sync module and then back to mobile app via Blink cloud).
Due to it must go through cloud (no local LAN mode), videos saved on cloud is more responsive than local storage. While you could pull out the USB stick and check the videos on a PC or laptop, it kinda defeats the purpose.
It struggles with WiFi smartconnect, especially with Asus routers. You either disable that or you setup a separate WiFi without smartconnect (2.4GHz and 5GHz configured separately).
App is far too restricted. Doesn't support multiple users. You can't disable notifications at camera level (it's either all on or all off).
Motion event only setup (which is the case for battery based Blink cameras) can miss events or have false positive events. Subscription ($$$) based smart detection kind of helps, but still not good enough.
The "Continue?" prompt is for battery based camera. It's there to avoid draining battery. However, it can get annoying. Should provide an option on how long to continue for, rather than regularly prompting every 60 seconds.
Without Internet, Blink devices are essentially offline (no LAN mode as mentioned above).
Uneven battery drain. On quite a few occasions, one battery will drain out first. Thing is, if you replace just that one, the other one will be next. Replacing both, given these are lithium AA batteries cost more.
However, they are better than $10 or less AliExpress junk class cameras.
[netsurfer] These might be okay if:
You are only after a doorbell that you mostly only care about getting notified when someone presses the bell. You also expect most people pressing your doorbell will stay in the visible area for a while.
No issue disabling WiFi smart connect on your router or willing to run a separate WiFi network (or guest network) for the Blink setup. Or, you are not even running WiFi 6 or better (so there is no smart connect support anyway).
Manually monitor an area (i.e. disable motion event and manually check it when needed).
As a motion triggered night light (Blink indoor camera / wired). You do need to setup another Blink account so you can block all notifications from that account.
Missing motion events for Blink outdoor 4 is okay to you (as you expect visitors will eventually press the doorbell).
You might not be able to setup 10+ cameras with your primary camera system so there could be some areas where you want to occasionally check (or to cover blind spots for the main camera system). For that purpose, Blink could be acceptable.
[shmahoo] I bought this a month or so ago and it's incredible value for the price. Images are good from the HD cameras.
I bought another item that came with a hub that can store to memory stick
I've avoided the monthly fee and making do with the free version
EDIT - just conditioning I bought the 2K version of these cameras. A MUCH nicer image than these ones, and they were still super cheap
[compound] Bought a few of these for the house. Ended up taking them out and replacing with TPLINK.
App is a pain to use. A lot of back and forth for the past year. Even harder when you're abroad with connection to your mobile number.
Lithium 1.5v drains in about a year, and not the two year as claimed. It's strange because the drain is only for one battery and the other one shows charge. This is for the two camera's I've set up in different states.
Subscription of $5 per camera, the usb flash drive to hub is slow and almost non useable because you'll need to go into the drive to access the videos…
Also detection software is trash, either too sensitive or too unresponsive.
[lothus777] Absolute junk, app takes forever to load, cant imagine what local storage takes
[Codeless] I have read a lot of negative reviews about it, does anyone have any other recommendations with a similar price to this?
[netsurfer] TP-Link is the next level up from this. Cost a bit more, but still quite affordable.
[yasocato] The newer version 2K+ is also discounted. 5 solar powered cameras for $234. I thought I'd give it a go since it's eligible for 30 day return via Amazon.
